title: Andryusha and Nervous Barriers
titleZh: 安德留沙与紧张的障碍物
statementMd:
Andryusha has found a perplexing arcade machine. The machine is a vertically adjusted board divided into square cells. The board has $*w*$ columns numbered from $1$ to $*w*$ from left to right, and $*h*$ rows numbered from $1$ to $*h*$ from the bottom to the top.

Further, there are barriers in some of board rows. There are $*n*$ barriers in total, and $*i*$-th of them occupied the cells $*l*_{*i*}$ through $*r*_{*i*}$ of the row $*u*_{*i*}$. Andryusha recollects well that no two barriers share the same row. Furthermore, no row is completely occupied with a barrier, that is, at least one cell in each row is free.

The player can throw a marble to any column of the machine from above. A marble falls downwards until it encounters a barrier, or falls through the bottom of the board. A marble disappears once it encounters a barrier but is replaced by two more marbles immediately to the left and to the right of the same barrier. In a situation when the barrier is at an edge of the board, both marbles appear next to the barrier at the side opposite to the edge. More than one marble can occupy the same place of the board, without obstructing each other's movement. Ultimately, all marbles are bound to fall from the bottom of the machine.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/be7f826a9594cfaaea0158d8904a494fe6296844.png) Examples of marble-barrier interaction.

Peculiarly, sometimes marbles can go through barriers as if they were free cells. That is so because the barriers are in fact alive, and frightened when a marble was coming at them from a very high altitude. More specifically, if a marble falls towards the barrier $*i*$ from relative height more than $*s*_{*i*}$ (that is, it started its fall strictly higher than $*u*_{*i*} + *s*_{*i*}$), then the barrier evades the marble. If a marble is thrown from the top of the board, it is considered to appear at height $(*h* + 1)$.

Andryusha remembers to have thrown a marble once in each of the columns. Help him find the total number of marbles that came down at the bottom of the machine. Since the answer may be large, print it modulo $10^{9} + 7$.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*h*$, $*w*$, and $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *h* ≤ 10^{9}$, $2 ≤ *w* ≤ 10^{5}$, $0 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$) — the number of rows, columns, and barriers in the machine respectively.

Next $*n*$ lines describe barriers. $*i*$-th of these lines containts four integers $*u*_{*i*}$, $*l*_{*i*}$, $*r*_{*i*}$, and $*s*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*i*} ≤ *h*$, $1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *w*$, $1 ≤ *s*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — row index, leftmost and rightmost column index of $*i*$-th barrier, and largest relative fall height such that the barrier does not evade a falling marble. It is guaranteed that each row has at least one free cell, and that all $*u*_{*i*}$ are distinct.

## Output

Print one integer — the answer to the problem modulo $10^{9} + 7$.

## Note

In the first sample case, there is a single barrier: if one throws a marble in the second or the third column, two marbles come out, otherwise there is only one. The total answer is $7$.

In the second sample case, the numbers of resulting marbles are $2$, $2$, $4$, $4$, $4$ in order of indexing columns with the initial marble.

In the third sample case, the numbers of resulting marbles are $1$, $1$, $4$, $4$, $4$. Note that the first barrier evades the marbles falling from the top of the board, but does not evade the marbles falling from the second barrier.

In the fourth sample case, the numbers of resulting marbles are $2$, $2$, $6$, $6$, $6$, $6$, $6$, $6$, $6$, $1$, $2$, $1$, $1$, $1$, $1$. The picture below shows the case when a marble is thrown into the seventh column.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f7b8f0edcdb3f141f20293b0002b5c7d561e06d8.png) The result of throwing a marble into the seventh column.
statementZhMd:
安德留沙发现了一台令人困惑的街机。机器是一块竖直放置的棋盘，被划分为方形格子。棋盘有 $*w*$ 列，从左到右编号为 $1$ 到 $*w*$；有 $*h*$ 行，从下到上编号为 $1$ 到 $*h*$。

此外，棋盘的某些行中存在障碍物。总共有 $*n*$ 个障碍物，其中第 $*i*$ 个障碍物占据第 $*u*_{*i*}$ 行中从 $*l*_{*i*}$ 列到 $*r*_{*i*}$ 列的格子。安德留沙清楚地记得，没有两个障碍物位于同一行。此外，没有任何一行被障碍物完全占据，也就是说，每一行至少有一个空闲格子。

玩家可以从机器上方将一颗弹珠投入任意一列。弹珠会向下落，直到遇到障碍物，或从棋盘底部落出。当弹珠遇到障碍物时，它会消失，同时在同一障碍物的正左侧和正右侧各出现一颗新的弹珠。如果障碍物位于棋盘边缘，两颗弹珠都会出现在障碍物另一侧、紧邻障碍物的位置。棋盘的同一位置可以有多颗弹珠，它们不会妨碍彼此的移动。最终，所有弹珠都会从机器底部落出。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/be7f826a9594cfaaea0158d8904a494fe6296844.png) 弹珠与障碍物交互的示例。

奇怪的是，有时弹珠可以像穿过空闲格子一样穿过障碍物。这是因为障碍物实际上是活的，当弹珠从非常高的地方向它们落来时，它们会受到惊吓。更具体地说，如果一颗弹珠朝着障碍物 $*i*$ 下落时的相对高度大于 $*s*_{*i*}$（也就是说，它开始下落的位置严格高于 $*u*_{*i*} + *s*_{*i*}$），那么障碍物就会躲开这颗弹珠。如果弹珠是从棋盘顶部投入的，则认为它出现在高度 $(*h* + 1)$ 处。

安德留沙记得，他曾经在每一列各投入过一颗弹珠。请帮助他求出最终从机器底部落出的弹珠总数。由于答案可能很大，请将其对 $10^{9} + 7$ 取模后输出。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $*h*$、$*w*$ 和 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *h* ≤ 10^{9}$，$2 ≤ *w* ≤ 10^{5}$，$0 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$），分别表示机器的行数、列数和障碍物数量。

接下来 $*n*$ 行描述障碍物。第 $*i*$ 行包含四个整数 $*u*_{*i*}$、$*l*_{*i*}$、$*r*_{*i*}$ 和 $*s*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *u*_{*i*} ≤ *h*$，$1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *w*$，$1 ≤ *s*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$），分别表示第 $*i*$ 个障碍物所在的行、其最左和最右列，以及该障碍物不会躲开下落弹珠时所允许的最大相对下落高度。保证每一行至少有一个空闲格子，并且所有 $*u*_{*i*}$ 互不相同。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即答案对 $10^{9} + 7$ 取模后的结果。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，只有一个障碍物：如果将弹珠投入第二列或第三列，则会有两颗弹珠落出；否则只有一颗。总答案为 $7$。

在第二个样例中，按照初始弹珠所在列的编号顺序，最终弹珠数量依次为 $2$、$2$、$4$、$4$、$4$。

在第三个样例中，最终弹珠数量依次为 $1$、$1$、$4$、$4$、$4$。注意，第一个障碍物会躲开从棋盘顶部落下的弹珠，但不会躲开从第二个障碍物处落下的弹珠。

在第四个样例中，最终弹珠数量依次为 $2$、$2$、$6$、$6$、$6$、$6$、$6$、$6$、$6$、$1$、$2$、$1$、$1$、$1$、$1$。下图展示了将一颗弹珠投入第七列时的情况。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f7b8f0edcdb3f141f20293b0002b5c7d561e06d8.png) 将弹珠投入第七列后的结果。
